INVESTIGATED at B5 under claim CB-0524 — the atlas page lazy-loads components/common/MapView (next/dynamic, ssr off) — the only runtime module load this page makes beyond the framework chunks. In-tree exercise, completed at head adc5a5911: (1) genus confirmed — all four lenses, and only they in this shape, lazy-load that one component; MapView is built on maplibre-gl v6, which loads further module/worker code at runtime. (2) No mis-typed asset route exists in this tree: next.config rewrites cover only /api and /socket.io (no catch-all to HTML), and the production server-proxy hands every other request to Next's own handler, so a chunk the serving build lacks is answered with Next's HTML 404 — which is exactly the browser's text/html module-MIME refusal. (3) Two candidate causes remain, both outside what code at this seat can settle: deploy staleness (page HTML and chunk inventory from different builds — the tickets' own suspected area) or a non-nonce-propagated module/worker load refused under the middleware's script-src 'strict-dynamic' (the middleware itself documents this exact failure class for the Studio lens's audioWorklet module load and carves an exception for it). (4) The deciding evidence is the failing URL, which sits in the audit's console screenshots (webp, Grok-side evidence tree) or a live repro — with the URL, the layer settles: a /_next/static chunk name means staleness (deploy lane), a worker/module path means the CSP shape (a middleware change, founder-visible, not a silent builder fix). Left OPEN for the desk/walker with this exercise; no fix invented.

A member's private mood check-in moved the shared affect state that chat, council and agent policy derive from. Mechanism, exercised end to end at branch state: the ATS middleware keys sessions per authenticated user (user_<id>, its own comment: prevents 'shared mood' across users) and server-internal reads use that session — but POST /api/affect/event and /api/affect/reset resolved the session from the request BODY first, and the affect lens's AffectSessionProvider defaulted its sessionId to the literal 'default', so MoodTracker's S-AFF-1 emit (and every panel read) landed in the one shared 'default' session; one check-in's FEEDBACK event (intensity 0.50, polarity +0.50) moved its Valence 50 to 56.2 with Arousal, Coherence and Trust — the ticket's exact numbers. Fix (cf8b787c5): both write routes now resolve req._atsSessionId FIRST (a body field can no longer steer a write into a shared or another user's session); the session context defaults to '' (no named session — reads fall back to the caller's own server-keyed session); the session strip's clear-field path returns to '' instead of 'default'. S-AFF-1's intent is preserved: your own state still moves with your own acts — it is no longer everyone's state. A deliberately named session can still be VIEWED (GET routes keep their param), but writes always land in the caller's own session. Pins: server/tests/affect-session-isolation.test.js 5/5 on the fixed tree, 1 pass / 4 fail on the pristine control (the pass is the unchanged middleware keying); affect-policy-derivations green; FE affect panels 3/4 in the borrowed env with the single failure (ChartKit render) proven identical on pristine files — pre-existing env noise. Reference shape matched: the platform-internal gate's server-mirrored identity rule (CB-0402) — the server, not the client, owns the caller's identity.

Invoice create and Mark paid posted no journal entries, no audit log, and no revenue or cash change — AR never reached the ledger. Premise exercised in code: invoice-create pushed only the invoice row and invoice-mark-paid only flipped its status, while the same domain file carries a complete double-entry journal (je-post with CoA validation, balance guard and recordAudit) the invoice actions never called. Fix: an internal postInvoiceJournal helper in je-post's exact entry shape (source 'accounting-invoice', sourceId = the invoice id, audit-logged via recordAudit) — invoice-create posts Dr Accounts Receivable (acct_1100) / Cr Sales Revenue (acct_4000) at the invoice total dated issuedAt and stamps invoice.journalEntryId; invoice-mark-paid posts Dr Cash (acct_1000) / Cr AR dated paidAt, refuses to double-post (a repeat mark-paid returns alreadyPaid with no entry), and books the recognition leg first for legacy invoices created before postings existed; invoice-void of an open invoice posts the reversal (Dr Revenue / Cr AR) so no phantom receivable or revenue survives. invoice-credit-note's journal leg is named, not built: it operates on already-paid invoices and its refund-payable account shape is a desk call. Tests: server/tests/accounting-invoice-journal.test.js 4/4 on the fixed tree and 0/4 on the pristine control; accounting-domain-parity stays green (95/95 together). Reference matched: the domain's own je-post entry + audit shape, no new machinery.

INVESTIGATED at B5 (slice premise-check) — the ticket's core charge is true and structural. Exercised end to end at branch state: the builder lets a user author workflows whose default trigger is 'button_click' (WorkflowBuilder, workflowSave), but NOTHING executes a workflow anywhere — there is no workflow-run action in server/domains/appmaker.js (only workflowOptions / workflowSave / workflowDelete), and previewRender emits purely static HTML: its button element is a handler-less <button> with no script in the document at all, inside an iframe sandboxed 'allow-same-origin' without allow-scripts. So a counter-style app (button + text) can be built and saved but its button can never act in the preview, which the app-maker build of record names the honest run surface ('RUN not built (no runtime)'). Building the missing piece is an app-runtime build — a workflow executor plus an interactive preview — with a real security shape to decide (user-authored logic executing in the preview frame; the current sandbox posture reads deliberate), not a sweep fix; priced here for the desk. Two adjacent facts from the same exercise: (1) data bindings are stored on the element expressly 'so previewRender can surface them' (dataBindElement) but renderEl never reads el.binding — a smaller unwired renderer leg the desk can scope separately; (2) the ticket's reload leg does not reproduce from code — editorSavePage persists elements faithfully (500 cap, props intact) and the canvas and preview both read the same saved pages, so the 'few shapes after reload' observation needs a live repro with the project id to chase further. Left OPEN with this exercise; no fix invented.

Transit stops lived only in TransitCoveragePanel's useState — parcels in the same workspace load from the persisted parcel store on mount, stops started empty every mount and were never saved, so a reload dropped every stop (the ticket's repro: analysis ran, stop absent after reload). Fix mirrors the lens's own parcel pattern (the matched in-product reference, and the ticket's stated expectation: 'Stop persists like parcels, scenarios and projects do'): server/domains/urbanplanning.js gains a per-user stops store in the same urbanPlanningLens state (stop-add with coordinate validation and a bounded mode set, stop-list, stop-remove — the parcel trio's exact shape, saveUpState on every mutation), and the panel loads stops on mount, adds through stop-add (speaking a save refusal inline instead of pretending), and removes through stop-remove. Evidence: new server/tests/urban-planning-stops-persist.test.js 4/4 (add→list round trip scoped per owner, invalid coordinates refused with nothing stored, mode fallback, remove + stranger not_found) against a 0/4 pristine control (actions unregistered before the fix); the existing urban-planning suites (full-build, lens-macros, mentalhealth parity) pass 81/81 with the fix. Panel render in the borrowed FE env NOT RUN this pass — the wiring follows the panel's existing lensRun load pattern for parcels line for line; the desk's CI plus the walker's re-pass govern the click-through.

INVESTIGATED at B5 (slice premise-check) — the symptom is accepted as filed (global search finds the created DTU, dtu_b9489555bd5a87b28f4c, while the lens's listIngested and local search return nothing and Recent DTUs reads 0). The lens-side code is coherent and exercised: WorkbenchPanel ingests via ingestText and reads via listIngested; ingestText creates chunk DTUs through ctx.macro dtu.create with domain 'ingest' and tags ['ingested']; listIngested/getIngested read STATE.dtus filtered by callerIngestedDtus — owner chain author||ownerId||userId||createdBy||authorId must equal the caller AND (tags includes 'ingested' OR domain === 'ingest'). The shipped ingest-full-build tests pass with a dtu.create stand-in whose header states the real macro's contract as stamping the caller as author — under that contract the round trip works, so the live divergence sits in what the production dtu.create actually stamps on macro-created DTUs (author field name/value, whether caller tags survive creation, whether domain is rewritten), inside the monolith's runMacro dispatch, which this pass traced to the dispatcher (makeCtx carries the caller; macro.run rebuilds ctx from the request) without convicting the create handler's field shape. Deciding probe, one look for whoever holds the live row or a local boot: read dtu_b9489555bd5a87b28f4c's author/ownerId/tags/domain and compare against the two chains above — whichever field mismatches is the fix site (stamp it in ingestText's create input if the macro honours inputs, or widen the reader's chains to the macro's actual stamp). Left OPEN with this exercise; no fix invented against an unread row.

Budget 'Spent' aggregated only the manual expense log — project-list's per-project spent and the dashboard's totalSpent both summed project.expenses and nothing else, while shopping-toggle flipped a purchased flag no aggregation read, so the walker's purchased  x 2 = 8 left Spent at /bin/bash exactly as filed. Fix makes the server the single aggregation source (matched reference: the lens's own shopping-list, which already totals purchased items as line totals): project-list now adds each project's purchased items (price x qty) into its spent with the portion exposed as shoppingSpent, and reports purchased items with no (or a deleted) project as unassignedShoppingSpent instead of dropping them; the dashboard's totalSpent includes all purchased shopping with shoppingSpent broken out. BudgetPanel's headline Spent adds the unassigned bucket to the per-project sum, so an unassigned purchase counts without inventing a project for it. Un-purchasing removes the amount again; manual expenses are untouched and cannot double-count a purchase (the toggle never wrote an expense). Evidence: new server/tests/home-improvement-shopping-spent.test.js 4/4 (the walker's exact 8 case, project-assigned roll-in, toggle-off reversal, expenses alongside purchases at 54 = 30 + 24) against a 0/4 pristine control; home-improvement parity suite green 25/25 in the same run.

The server round trip was never broken — driven in the harness, experiment-log appends {epoch:1, trainLoss:0.9} and experiment-list returns it. The defect was the manual form's Record button in ExperimentTracker: disabled until ALL THREE fields (train loss, val loss, accuracy) were filled, with nothing saying so, so the walker's repro (enter train loss 0.9, click Record) silently did nothing and epoch stayed 0 with an empty chart. The server's experiment-log accepts any subset and defaults the rest (its matched contract), so the form now enables Record when at least one field holds a finite number, names that requirement in the button title, and sends only the fields actually entered. Evidence: new components/ml/__tests__/ExperimentTracker.manual-log.test.tsx drives the real form against an in-memory store — Record starts disabled, enables on a lone train loss, logs with trainLoss only (valLoss/accuracy absent), and the epoch advances to 1/10 after reload; it fails on the pristine panel (Record never enables) and passes with the fix, with the full MlPanels coverage suite green 26/26 in the same env run.
